body.heading: Get ready before it starts
paragraphs: A sunset show starts before the sun goes down. Sit somewhere comfortable with your adult where you can see a wide piece of sky.
Have your pencils ready. The colours change quickly, and the best ones sometimes last only a minute or two.

body.heading: Name the colours
paragraphs: Watch the sky and clouds. Say each colour you see out loud — gold, peach, pink, purple, grey-blue. Make a quick scribble of each colour on your paper in order.
Clouds are the sunset's screen. They catch the light and turn pink and orange even after the ground below is in shadow.

body.heading: The quiet ending
paragraphs: After the sun dips away, the sky fades slowly through purple to deep blue. The first stars may appear while a line of orange still glows.
Your diary page now holds one evening forever. No two sunsets ever paint the exact same picture.

takeaway: A sunset changes colour minute by minute, and a colour diary catches the show before it fades.
safetyNotes: Never look straight at the Sun, even at sunset. Look at the sky and clouds around it instead.
screenFreeExtension: Make a sunset strip at home — colour a long strip of paper in the order the colours appeared.
